typedef enum
{
  ELF_C_NULL,            /* Nothing, terminate, or compute only.  */
  ELF_C_READ,            /* Read .. */
  ELF_C_RDWR,            /* Read and write .. */
  ELF_C_WRITE,           /* Write .. */
  ELF_C_CLR,             /* Clear flag.  */
  ELF_C_SET,             /* Set flag.  */
  ELF_C_FDDONE,          /* Signal that file descriptor will not be
                             used anymore.  */
  ELF_C_FDREAD,          /* Read rest of data so that file descriptor
                             is not used anymore.  */
  /* The following are extensions.  */
  ELF_C_READ_MMAP,       /* Read, but mmap the file if possible.  */
  ELF_C_RDWR_MMAP,       /* Read and write, with mmap.  */
  ELF_C_WRITE_MMAP,      /* Write, with mmap.  */
  ELF_C_READ_MMAP_PRIVATE, /* Read, but memory is writable, results are
                               not written to the file.  */
  ELF_C_EMPTY,           /* Copy basic file data but not the content. */
  /* Keep this the last entry.  */
  ELF_C_NUM
} Elf_Cmd;

functions.name: elf_begin
functions.description: Open or attach to an ELF file and return a descriptor that will operate according to the command (read, write, etc.). Use a file descriptor and, optionally, a reference descriptor (e.g., for archive iteration).
requirements: __fildes must be a valid open file descriptor referring to the target file.
__cmd must be a valid Elf_Cmd value appropriate for how the descriptor will be used (e.g., ELF_C_READ/ELF_C_RDWR/ELF_C_WRITE, or mmap variants).
__ref may be NULL for an initial open; when iterating archives, a valid existing Elf* is expected (details are not specified in this header).
On failure, callers should check elf_errno() or elf_errmsg(0) for error details.

functions.name: elf_clone
functions.description: Create a clone of an existing ELF descriptor with the specified access/operation mode.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf* previously obtained (e.g., from elf_begin/elf_memory).
__cmd must be a valid Elf_Cmd for the intended access semantics.
On failure, NULL is returned and elf_errno is set.

functions.name: elf_memory
functions.description: Create an ELF descriptor that treats the given memory buffer as an ELF object image.
requirements: __image must point to a memory buffer containing an ELF or archive image; buffer must remain valid for the lifetime of the Elf* descriptor.
__size must be the total size in bytes of the image buffer and nonzero.
On failure, NULL is returned and elf_errno is set.

functions.name: elf_next
functions.description: Advance an archive descriptor to the next element. Returns a command indicating the next action or state.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf* referring to an archive (ELF_K_AR).
Return value should be checked to drive iteration or detect end/errors; consult elf_errno on error.

functions.name: elf_end
functions.description: Free resources allocated for an ELF descriptor. After this call, the descriptor and any pointers derived from it must not be used.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf* or NULL (behavior for NULL is unspecified in this header).
Call exactly once per successful elf_begin/elf_memory/elf_clone to avoid leaks; after calling, do not reuse __elf or derived objects.
Return value should be checked; on failure, elf_errno is set.

functions.name: elf_update
functions.description: Update the ELF descriptor’s state and optionally write changes to disk, depending on the command.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf*; if writing, it must have been opened with a writable mode (e.g., ELF_C_RDWR/ELF_C_WRITE).
__cmd must be an appropriate Elf_Cmd for update (e.g., compute-only or write; specific semantics not detailed in this header).
Return value should be checked; negative return sets elf_errno.

functions.name: elf_kind
functions.description: Return the kind of object associated with the descriptor (unknown, archive, COFF, or ELF).
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf* (may be NULL to query nothing; behavior not detailed here).
Pure function w.r.t. arguments; does not modify state.

functions.name: elf_getbase
functions.description: Get the base offset for an object file within its container (e.g., within an archive).
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf*.
Return value should be checked for errors; on failure elf_errno is set.

functions.name: elf_getident
functions.description: Retrieve a pointer to the file identification (e_ident) bytes for the object, along with the buffer length.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf*.
__nbytes must be a valid pointer where the number of bytes will be stored.
Returned pointer is owned by the library; lifetime is tied to the Elf* and becomes invalid after elf_end.

functions.name: elf32_getehdr
functions.description: Return a pointer to the 32-bit ELF header (Ehdr) for the object, if applicable to ELFCLASS32.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf* of class ELFCLASS32; if the file is ELFCLASS64, use elf64_getehdr.
Returned pointer is managed by the library and may be invalidated by other operations (e.g., compression or update as noted elsewhere).
On failure, NULL is returned and elf_errno is set.

functions.name: elf64_getehdr
functions.description: Return a pointer to the 64-bit ELF header (Ehdr) for the object, if applicable to ELFCLASS64.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf* of class ELFCLASS64; if the file is ELFCLASS32, use elf32_getehdr.
Returned pointer is managed by the library and may be invalidated by other operations.
On failure, NULL is returned and elf_errno is set.

functions.name: elf32_newehdr
functions.description: Create and attach a new 32-bit ELF header to the object if none exists, and return it.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf* intended to be ELFCLASS32.
Behavior is undefined if a header already exists; on failure or invalid class, NULL is returned and elf_errno is set.
Caller should set necessary header fields before writing/updating.

functions.name: elf64_newehdr
functions.description: Create and attach a new 64-bit ELF header to the object if none exists, and return it.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf* intended to be ELFCLASS64.
Behavior is undefined if a header already exists; on failure or invalid class, NULL is returned and elf_errno is set.
Caller should set necessary header fields before writing/updating.

functions.name: elf_getphdrnum
functions.description: Get the number of program headers for the ELF file, using e_phnum or, if extended, sh_info of section 0.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf*.
__dst must be a valid pointer where the count will be stored.
Returns 0 on success; on error returns -1 and sets elf_errno (conventional libelf behavior, implied).

functions.name: elf32_getphdr
functions.description: Return the program header table for a 32-bit ELF object.
requirements: __elf must be a valid ELFCLASS32 descriptor; use elf64_getphdr for 64-bit.
On failure, NULL is returned and elf_errno is set.

functions.name: elf64_getphdr
functions.description: Return the program header table for a 64-bit ELF object.
requirements: __elf must be a valid ELFCLASS64 descriptor; use elf32_getphdr for 32-bit.
On failure, NULL is returned and elf_errno is set.

functions.name: elf32_newphdr
functions.description: Create a new 32-bit program header table with the given number of entries and attach it to the object.
requirements: __elf must be a valid ELFCLASS32 descriptor.
__cnt is the number of program headers to create; must be appropriate for the object (exact limits are not specified here).
On failure, NULL is returned and elf_errno is set.

functions.name: elf64_newphdr
functions.description: Create a new 64-bit program header table with the given number of entries and attach it to the object.
requirements: __elf must be a valid ELFCLASS64 descriptor.
__cnt is the number of program headers to create; must be appropriate for the object (exact limits are not specified here).
On failure, NULL is returned and elf_errno is set.

functions.name: elf_getscn
functions.description: Return the section descriptor at the given index.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf* and __index must be a valid section index.
On failure, NULL is returned and elf_errno is set.

functions.name: elf32_offscn
functions.description: Return the section descriptor that starts at the given 32-bit file offset for a 32-bit ELF object.
requirements: __elf must be a valid ELFCLASS32 descriptor.
__offset must correspond to the start of a section; otherwise NULL is returned and elf_errno is set.

functions.name: elf64_offscn
functions.description: Return the section descriptor that starts at the given 64-bit file offset for a 64-bit ELF object.
requirements: __elf must be a valid ELFCLASS64 descriptor.
__offset must correspond to the start of a section; otherwise NULL is returned and elf_errno is set.

functions.name: elf_ndxscn
functions.description: Return the index of the provided section descriptor.
requirements: __scn must be a valid section descriptor.
On error or NULL input, the function may return a sentinel (not specified here); check elf_errno if needed.

functions.name: elf_nextscn
functions.description: Return the next section after the provided one, or the first section if __scn is NULL.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf*.
If __scn is non-NULL, it must be a section of __elf.
On failure or end, NULL may be returned; check elf_errno to distinguish.

functions.name: elf_newscn
functions.description: Create a new section and append it to the section table, returning its descriptor.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf* opened with a mode that allows modification if persisting changes is intended.
On failure, NULL is returned and elf_errno is set.

functions.name: elf_scnshndx
functions.description: Return the section index of the extended section index table (SHT_SYMTAB_SHNDX) linked to the given symbol table section, or codes per the comment.
requirements: __scn must be a valid section descriptor; if NULL, returns -1 and sets elf_errno.
Returns 0 if __scn is not a symbol table or no extended index table is found; otherwise returns the section index; on error returns -1 and sets elf_errno.

functions.name: elf_getshdrnum
functions.description: Get the number of sections in the ELF file, using e_shnum or, if extended, sh_size of section 0.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf*.
__dst must be a valid pointer where the section count will be stored.
Returns 0 on success; returns -1 and sets elf_errno on error.

functions.name: elf_getshnum
functions.description: Deprecated alias for retrieving the number of sections; use elf_getshdrnum instead.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf*.
__dst must be a valid pointer.
Deprecated: new code should prefer elf_getshdrnum.
Returns 0 on success; returns -1 and sets elf_errno on error.

functions.name: elf_getshdrstrndx
functions.description: Get the section index of the section header string table (shstrtab), using e_shstrndx or, if extended, sh_link of section 0.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf*.
__dst must be a valid pointer where the index will be stored.
Returns 0 on success; returns -1 and sets elf_errno on error.

functions.name: elf_getshstrndx
functions.description: Deprecated alias for retrieving the shstrtab section index; use elf_getshdrstrndx instead.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf*.
__dst must be a valid pointer.
Deprecated: prefer elf_getshdrstrndx.
Returns 0 on success; returns -1 and sets elf_errno on error.

functions.name: elf32_getshdr
functions.description: Return the 32-bit section header for the given section.
requirements: __scn must be a valid section descriptor of an ELFCLASS32 object.
On failure, NULL is returned and elf_errno is set.

functions.name: elf64_getshdr
functions.description: Return the 64-bit section header for the given section.
requirements: __scn must be a valid section descriptor of an ELFCLASS64 object.
On failure, NULL is returned and elf_errno is set.

functions.name: elf32_getchdr
functions.description: If the section’s data is compressed, return its 32-bit compression header; otherwise return NULL and set elf_errno.
requirements: __scn must be a valid section descriptor.
Section must be compressed; if not compressed or on error, returns NULL and sets elf_errno.

functions.name: elf64_getchdr
functions.description: If the section’s data is compressed, return its 64-bit compression header; otherwise return NULL and set elf_errno.
requirements: __scn must be a valid section descriptor.
Section must be compressed; if not compressed or on error, returns NULL and sets elf_errno.

functions.name: elf_compress
functions.signature: extern int elf_compress (Elf_Scn *scn, int type, unsigned int flags);
functions.description: Compress or decompress a section’s data using ELF section compression (SHF_COMPRESSED with an Elf*_Chdr header). Manages SHF_COMPRESSED and adjusts section data accordingly.
requirements: scn must be a valid section descriptor.
type must be 0 to request decompression, or an ELFCOMPRESS_* algorithm (e.g., ELFCOMPRESS_ZLIB or ELFCOMPRESS_ZSTD) to request compression.
flags may be 0 or include ELF_CHF_FORCE to force compression even if size would not be reduced.
It is an error to request compression for a section that already has SHF_COMPRESSED set.
It is an error to request decompression for a section that does not have SHF_COMPRESSED set.
It is always an error to call on SHT_NOBITS sections or sections with SHF_ALLOC set.
All previously returned Shdrs and Elf_Data for this section are invalidated by a successful call.
On success returns 1; if compression is requested but would not reduce size (and not forced), returns 0; on error returns -1 and sets elf_errno.
Changes are not automatically marked dirty; to persist with elf_update, mark the section ELF_F_DIRTY.

functions.name: elf_compress_gnu
functions.signature: extern int elf_compress_gnu (Elf_Scn *scn, int compress, unsigned int flags);
functions.description: Compress or decompress a section using the legacy GNU debug section compression format (traditionally for .debug*/.zdebug*), storing only uncompressed size.
requirements: scn must be a valid section descriptor.
compress must be 1 to request compression or 0 to request decompression.
flags may be 0 or include ELF_CHF_FORCE to force compression even if size would not be reduced.
If a section has SHF_COMPRESSED set, calling elf_compress_gnu is an error; first decompress using elf_compress.
elf_compress can be used on sections previously compressed with elf_compress_gnu, though it is typically unnecessary.
It is always an error to call on SHT_NOBITS sections or sections with SHF_ALLOC set.
elf_compress_gnu does not check section naming; caller is responsible for only using it on appropriately named sections and renaming as needed.
All previously returned Shdrs and Elf_Data for this section are invalidated by a successful call.
On success returns 1; if (not forced) compression would not reduce size, returns 0; on error returns -1 and sets elf_errno.
Changes are not automatically marked dirty; mark the section ELF_F_DIRTY to persist.

functions.name: elf_flagelf
functions.signature: extern unsigned int elf_flagelf (Elf *__elf, Elf_Cmd __cmd, unsigned int __flags);
functions.description: Set or clear flags on the ELF file descriptor, depending on the command.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf*.
__cmd must be ELF_C_SET to set or ELF_C_CLR to clear the provided flags.
__flags is a bitmask of ELF_F_* flags (e.g., ELF_F_DIRTY, ELF_F_LAYOUT, ELF_F_PERMISSIVE).
Returns the resulting flags.

functions.name: elf_flagehdr
functions.signature: extern unsigned int elf_flagehdr (Elf *__elf, Elf_Cmd __cmd, unsigned int __flags);
functions.description: Set or clear flags on the ELF header associated with the descriptor, depending on the command.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf*.
__cmd must be ELF_C_SET or ELF_C_CLR.
__flags is a bitmask of applicable flags (ELF_F_*).
Returns the resulting flags.

functions.name: elf_flagphdr
functions.signature: extern unsigned int elf_flagphdr (Elf *__elf, Elf_Cmd __cmd, unsigned int __flags);
functions.description: Set or clear flags on the ELF program header table, depending on the command.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf*.
__cmd must be ELF_C_SET or ELF_C_CLR.
__flags is a bitmask of applicable flags (ELF_F_*).
Returns the resulting flags.

functions.name: elf_flagscn
functions.signature: extern unsigned int elf_flagscn (Elf_Scn *__scn, Elf_Cmd __cmd, unsigned int __flags);
functions.description: Set or clear flags on the specified section descriptor, depending on the command.
requirements: __scn must be a valid section descriptor.
__cmd must be ELF_C_SET or ELF_C_CLR.
__flags is a bitmask of applicable flags (ELF_F_*).
Returns the resulting flags.

functions.name: elf_flagdata
functions.signature: extern unsigned int elf_flagdata (Elf_Data *__data, Elf_Cmd __cmd, unsigned int __flags);
functions.description: Set or clear flags on the specified data buffer descriptor, depending on the command.
requirements: __data must be a valid Elf_Data pointer obtained from libelf.
__cmd must be ELF_C_SET or ELF_C_CLR.
__flags is a bitmask of applicable flags (ELF_F_*).
Returns the resulting flags.

functions.name: elf_flagshdr
functions.signature: extern unsigned int elf_flagshdr (Elf_Scn *__scn, Elf_Cmd __cmd, unsigned int __flags);
functions.description: Set or clear flags on the section header associated with the given section, depending on the command.
requirements: __scn must be a valid section descriptor.
__cmd must be ELF_C_SET or ELF_C_CLR.
__flags is a bitmask of applicable flags (ELF_F_*).
Returns the resulting flags.

functions.name: elf_getdata
functions.description: Translate and return data from a section in memory representation. d_type is set based on sh_type, or to ELF_T_CHDR for compressed sections.
requirements: __scn must be a valid section descriptor.
__data is used to iterate section data chunks (conventional libelf usage); passing NULL retrieves the first chunk (not explicitly stated here).
Returned Elf_Data pointer’s lifetime is tied to the section/ELF descriptor; previous buffers might be invalidated by operations like compression.
On failure, returns NULL and sets elf_errno.

functions.name: elf_rawdata
functions.description: Return uninterpreted (raw) section contents as data buffers in file representation.
requirements: __scn must be a valid section descriptor.
__data is used to iterate raw data chunks (conventional libelf usage; not explicitly documented here).
On failure, returns NULL and sets elf_errno.

functions.name: elf_newdata
functions.description: Create a new, empty data descriptor attached to the section for caller-populated content.
requirements: __scn must be a valid section descriptor; the ELF must be opened in a mode that allows modification to persist changes.
Returned Elf_Data must be filled with appropriate fields (buffer, size, alignment, type) before updating/writing.
On failure, returns NULL and sets elf_errno.

functions.name: elf_getdata_rawchunk
functions.description: Return a data descriptor for a raw chunk of the file of given type, translated as section data would be for that type. Valid until elf_end(ELF).
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf*.
__offset and __size must specify a valid range within the file image; out-of-range values result in error.
__type must be a valid Elf_Type describing how to interpret/translate the data.
On failure, returns NULL and sets elf_errno.

functions.name: elf_strptr
functions.description: Return a pointer to a string at the given offset within the string table section at the given index.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf*.
__index must be the section index of a valid string table (.strtab or .shstrtab).
__offset must be within the bounds of that string table; otherwise NULL is returned and elf_errno is set.
Returned pointer is managed by libelf and tied to the Elf* lifetime.

functions.name: elf_getarhdr
functions.description: Return the archive member header describing the current element when iterating an archive.
requirements: __elf must be a valid archive element descriptor (ELF_K_AR).
On failure, returns NULL and sets elf_errno.
Returned pointers to strings in the header are managed by libelf.

functions.name: elf_getaroff
functions.description: Return the archive offset for the current file within an archive.
requirements: __elf must be a valid archive descriptor or archive member descriptor.
Check return value for errors; on failure elf_errno is set.

functions.name: elf_rand
functions.description: Select the archive element at the given offset for an archive descriptor.
requirements: __elf must be a valid archive descriptor (ELF_K_AR).
__offset must denote a valid member’s offset within the archive; invalid offsets cause an error (return semantics not specified here, check elf_errno).

functions.name: elf_getarsym
functions.description: Return the archive symbol table and set the number of entries.
requirements: __elf must be a valid archive descriptor.
__narsyms must be a valid pointer to receive the number of symbols.
On failure, returns NULL and sets elf_errno.

functions.name: elf_cntl
functions.description: Control operations on an ELF descriptor (e.g., FDDONE/FDREAD to manage underlying fd usage).
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf*.
__cmd must be a valid control command, e.g., ELF_C_FDDONE or ELF_C_FDREAD as defined in Elf_Cmd.
Return value should be checked; on failure elf_errno is set.

functions.name: elf_rawfile
functions.description: Retrieve a pointer to the uninterpreted file contents and their length.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf*.
__nbytes must be a valid pointer to receive the file size in bytes.
Returned buffer pointer is managed by libelf and valid while the descriptor lives.

functions.name: elf32_fsize
functions.signature: extern size_t elf32_fsize (Elf_Type __type, size_t __count, unsigned int __version);
functions.description: Return the total size in bytes of an array of COUNT elements of TYPE in the external (file) representation for ELFCLASS32 under the given ELF version.
requirements: __type must be a valid Elf_Type.
__count is the number of elements; multiplication must not overflow size_t (undefined otherwise).
__version must be a valid ELF version constant (e.g., EV_CURRENT).
Function is const/pure w.r.t. inputs.

functions.name: elf64_fsize
functions.signature: extern size_t elf64_fsize (Elf_Type __type, size_t __count, unsigned int __version);
functions.description: Return the total size in bytes of an array of COUNT elements of TYPE in the external (file) representation for ELFCLASS64 under the given ELF version.
requirements: __type must be a valid Elf_Type.
__count is the number of elements; multiplication must not overflow size_t.
__version must be a valid ELF version constant (e.g., EV_CURRENT).
Function is const/pure w.r.t. inputs.

functions.name: elf32_xlatetom
functions.signature: extern Elf_Data *elf32_xlatetom (Elf_Data *__dest, const Elf_Data *__src, unsigned int __encode);
functions.description: Convert data from file representation to memory representation for ELFCLASS32 according to the specified encoding.
requirements: __dest must be a valid, writable Elf_Data structure and buffer; fields must be set appropriately (unknown specifics in this header).
__src must be a valid Elf_Data describing source data in file representation.
__encode selects byte encoding/endianness (exact values not specified here).
On failure, returns NULL and sets elf_errno.

functions.name: elf64_xlatetom
functions.signature: extern Elf_Data *elf64_xlatetom (Elf_Data *__dest, const Elf_Data *__src, unsigned int __encode);
functions.description: Convert data from file representation to memory representation for ELFCLASS64 according to the specified encoding.
requirements: __dest must be a valid, writable Elf_Data structure and buffer; fields must be set appropriately (unknown specifics in this header).
__src must be a valid Elf_Data describing source data in file representation.
__encode selects byte encoding/endianness (exact values not specified here).
On failure, returns NULL and sets elf_errno.

functions.name: elf32_xlatetof
functions.signature: extern Elf_Data *elf32_xlatetof (Elf_Data *__dest, const Elf_Data *__src, unsigned int __encode);
functions.description: Convert data from memory representation to file representation for ELFCLASS32 according to the specified encoding.
requirements: __dest must be a valid, writable Elf_Data structure and buffer; fields must be set appropriately (unknown specifics in this header).
__src must be a valid Elf_Data describing source data in memory representation.
__encode selects byte encoding/endianness (exact values not specified here).
On failure, returns NULL and sets elf_errno.

functions.name: elf64_xlatetof
functions.signature: extern Elf_Data *elf64_xlatetof (Elf_Data *__dest, const Elf_Data *__src, unsigned int __encode);
functions.description: Convert data from memory representation to file representation for ELFCLASS64 according to the specified encoding.
requirements: __dest must be a valid, writable Elf_Data structure and buffer; fields must be set appropriately (unknown specifics in this header).
__src must be a valid Elf_Data describing source data in memory representation.
__encode selects byte encoding/endianness (exact values not specified here).
On failure, returns NULL and sets elf_errno.

functions.name: elf_errno
functions.description: Return the thread-local error code from the most recent failing libelf call.
requirements: No arguments; callers should use immediately after a failing libelf function to retrieve the error code.
Thread-local: each thread maintains its own last error.

functions.name: elf_errmsg
functions.description: Return a human-readable error string. If __error is 0, return the message for the most recent error or NULL if none. If __error is -1, always return a legal (non-NULL) string for the last error state.
requirements: __error controls behavior: 0 for last error message, -1 for guaranteed non-NULL message, or a specific error code.
Returned string is managed by libelf; do not free.

functions.name: elf_version
functions.description: Coordinate libelf’s internal version with the application’s expected ELF version; returns the current library version.
requirements: __version should be set by the application to the ELF version it expects (e.g., EV_CURRENT).
Call early in program initialization to ensure version compatibility (common practice; not mandated here).

functions.name: elf_fill
functions.description: Set the byte value used by libelf to fill holes in data structures it creates or updates.
requirements: __fill is the fill byte value; exact valid range is not specified here (commonly 0–255).
Affects subsequent structure creation/update behavior.

functions.name: elf_hash
functions.signature: extern unsigned long int elf_hash (const char *__string);
functions.description: Compute the System V ELF hash value for a NUL-terminated symbol name string.
requirements: __string must be a valid NUL-terminated C string pointer.
Function is pure (does not modify state).

functions.name: elf_gnu_hash
functions.signature: extern unsigned long int elf_gnu_hash (const char *__string);
functions.description: Compute the GNU-style hash value for a NUL-terminated symbol name string.
requirements: __string must be a valid NUL-terminated C string pointer.
Function is pure (does not modify state).

functions.name: elf32_checksum
functions.description: Compute a simple checksum over the permanent parts of a 32-bit ELF file.
requirements: __elf must be a valid ELFCLASS32 descriptor.
On failure, a negative value may be returned and elf_errno set (exact semantics not detailed here).

functions.name: elf64_checksum
functions.description: Compute a simple checksum over the permanent parts of a 64-bit ELF file.
requirements: __elf must be a valid ELFCLASS64 descriptor.
On failure, a negative value may be returned and elf_errno set (exact semantics not detailed here).

functions.name: gelf_getclass
functions.description: Returns the ELF class (ELFCLASS32 or ELFCLASS64) for the given Elf handle. Use to detect whether an object is 32-bit or 64-bit. Returns an int class code defined by libelf.
requirements: __elf must be a valid, initialized Elf* obtained from libelf (e.g., via elf_begin).
The underlying file must be an ELF object; otherwise the class may be undefined or an error may be set.

functions.name: gelf_fsize
functions.signature: extern size_t gelf_fsize (Elf *__elf, Elf_Type __type, size_t __count, unsigned int __version);
functions.description: Computes the total size in bytes of an array of __count elements of the given ELF TYPE as it would appear in the file (external representation), using the class of __elf and the specified ELF standard version. Useful for sizing buffers when reading/writing ELF data blocks.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf*.
__type must be a valid Elf_Type corresponding to the data you are sizing.
__count is the number of elements; large values may overflow size_t if product exceeds representable range.
__version must be a valid ELF version constant accepted by libelf (e.g., EV_CURRENT).

functions.name: gelf_getehdr
functions.description: Retrieves the ELF file header into __dest in the generic 64-bit layout (GElf_Ehdr) regardless of file class. Returns __dest on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf* for an ELF file with a present file header.
__dest must be a non-null pointer to writable GElf_Ehdr storage.
The underlying object must have an ELF header; otherwise NULL is returned and elf_errno is set.

functions.name: gelf_update_ehdr
functions.description: Updates the ELF file header of __elf from the generic GElf_Ehdr provided in __src, converting to the native class as needed. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: __elf must be a valid, writable Elf* opened for updating.
__src must be a non-null pointer to a fully initialized GElf_Ehdr containing valid header fields for the target class.
The ELF kind must support having an ELF header; errors are reported via return value and elf_errno.

functions.name: gelf_newehdr
functions.description: Creates a new ELF header for the object if none exists, using the specified class (ELFCLASS32 or ELFCLASS64). Returns a pointer to the created class-specific header (Elf32_Ehdr or Elf64_Ehdr) or NULL on error.
requirements: __elf must be a valid, writable Elf* that currently has no ELF header.
__class must be ELFCLASS32 or ELFCLASS64.
Caller must check for NULL return and elf_errno on failure before using the result.

functions.name: gelf_offscn
functions.description: Returns the section descriptor at the given file offset within the ELF file, or NULL if none exists or on error. Useful to map a file offset to a section.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf*.
__offset is a file offset within the ELF; it should correspond to a section header's sh_offset.
Caller must check for NULL return and elf_errno to distinguish errors from 'not found'.

functions.name: gelf_getshdr
functions.description: Retrieves the section header for the given section into __dst as a generic GElf_Shdr, independent of class. Returns __dst on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: __scn must be a valid Elf_Scn* section descriptor.
__dst must be a non-null pointer to writable GElf_Shdr.
The section must have a header; otherwise NULL is returned and elf_errno is set.

functions.name: gelf_update_shdr
functions.description: Updates the section header for the given section from the provided generic GElf_Shdr, converting as needed. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: __scn must be a valid, writable section descriptor associated with a writable Elf object.
__src must be a non-null pointer to an initialized GElf_Shdr with valid field values for that section.
Caller must check return value and may inspect elf_errno on failure.

functions.name: gelf_getphdr
functions.description: Retrieves the program header table entry at index __ndx into __dst as a generic GElf_Phdr. Returns __dst on success or NULL on error.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf* with a program header table.
__ndx must be a valid index in [0, phnum).
__dst must be a non-null pointer to writable GElf_Phdr.
Caller must verify non-NULL return; errors are reported via elf_errno.

functions.name: gelf_update_phdr
functions.description: Updates the program header table entry at index __ndx from the generic GElf_Phdr provided. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: __elf must be a valid, writable Elf* with an existing program header table.
__ndx must be within the range of existing program headers.
__src must be a non-null pointer to an initialized GElf_Phdr.
Caller must check the return value and elf_errno on failure.

functions.name: gelf_newphdr
functions.description: Creates or replaces the program header table of the object with __phnum entries, using the object's class to allocate either Elf32_Phdr or Elf64_Phdr. Returns a pointer to the created table or NULL on error.
requirements: __elf must be a valid, writable Elf*.
__phnum is the desired number of program headers; large values must fit in memory and class limits.
Existing program header state may be replaced; caller should not hold stale pointers to prior phdr tables.
Caller must check for NULL and elf_errno on failure.

functions.name: gelf_getchdr
functions.description: Retrieves the compressed section header (chdr) of a section if it is compressed. Returns __dst on success, or NULL and sets elf_errno if the section is not compressed or an error occurs.
requirements: __scn must be a valid section descriptor.
__dst must be a non-null pointer to writable GElf_Chdr.
Section must be compressed for success; otherwise NULL is returned and elf_errno is set.

functions.name: gelf_xlatetom
functions.signature: extern Elf_Data *gelf_xlatetom (Elf *__elf, Elf_Data *__dest, const Elf_Data *__src, unsigned int __encode);
functions.description: Converts data from file representation to memory representation according to the class/endianness of __elf. The source is __src; the converted result is placed into __dest. __encode specifies the data encoding (e.g., ELFDATA2LSB or ELFDATA2MSB). Returns __dest on success or NULL on error.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf* that determines class and layout.
__dest must point to an Elf_Data buffer descriptor prepared for output; its buffer must be sufficiently large to hold the converted data.
__src must be a valid Elf_Data descriptor containing file-representation data of the indicated type/size.
__encode must be a valid ELF data encoding constant accepted by libelf.
Caller must check for NULL return and elf_errno on failure.

functions.name: gelf_xlatetof
functions.signature: extern Elf_Data *gelf_xlatetof (Elf *__elf, Elf_Data *__dest, const Elf_Data *__src, unsigned int __encode);
functions.description: Converts data from memory representation to file representation based on the class/endianness of __elf. The converted data is written into __dest. __encode selects the target encoding (e.g., ELFDATA2LSB or ELFDATA2MSB). Returns __dest on success or NULL on error.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf*.
__dest must be an Elf_Data descriptor with a buffer large enough for the converted data.
__src must be a valid Elf_Data in memory representation of the specified type/size.
__encode must be a valid ELF data encoding constant.
Caller must check for NULL return and elf_errno on failure.

functions.name: gelf_getrel
functions.description: Retrieves the REL relocation entry at index __ndx from the data block into __dst as a generic GElf_Rel. Returns __dst on success or NULL on error.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data from a section of type SHT_REL.
__ndx must be within the number of REL entries in __data.
__dst must be a non-null pointer to writable GElf_Rel.
Caller must check for NULL return and elf_errno on failure.

functions.name: gelf_getrela
functions.description: Retrieves the RELA relocation entry at index __ndx from the data block into __dst as a generic GElf_Rela. Returns __dst on success or NULL on error.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data from a section of type SHT_RELA.
__ndx must be within the number of RELA entries in __data.
__dst must be a non-null pointer to writable GElf_Rela.

functions.name: gelf_update_rel
functions.description: Updates the REL relocation entry at index __ndx in the data block from the provided GElf_Rel. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: __dst must be an Elf_Data for a writable SHT_REL section with enough space for the entry.
__ndx must be within bounds of the REL table.
__src must be a non-null pointer to an initialized GElf_Rel.
Caller must check return value and elf_errno on failure.

functions.name: gelf_update_rela
functions.description: Updates the RELA relocation entry at index __ndx in the data block from the provided GElf_Rela. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: __dst must be an Elf_Data for a writable SHT_RELA section with sufficient space.
__ndx must be within bounds of the RELA table.
__src must be a non-null pointer to an initialized GElf_Rela.

functions.name: gelf_getsym
functions.description: Retrieves the symbol table entry at index __ndx into __dst as a generic GElf_Sym. Returns __dst on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data from a SHT_SYMTAB or SHT_DYNSYM section.
__ndx must be within the number of symbols in __data.
__dst must be a non-null pointer to writable GElf_Sym.

functions.name: gelf_update_sym
functions.description: Updates the symbol table entry at index __ndx from the provided GElf_Sym. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data for a writable symbol table section (SHT_SYMTAB or SHT_DYNSYM).
__ndx must be within bounds of the symbol table.
__src must be a non-null pointer to an initialized GElf_Sym.

functions.name: gelf_getsymshndx
functions.signature: extern GElf_Sym *gelf_getsymshndx (Elf_Data *__symdata, Elf_Data *__shndxdata, int __ndx, GElf_Sym *__sym, Elf32_Word *__xshndx);
functions.description: Retrieves a symbol table entry and its associated extended section index at index __ndx. Populates __sym with the symbol and __xshndx with the extended section index. Returns __sym on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: __symdata must be an Elf_Data from a symbol table.
__shndxdata must be an Elf_Data from the corresponding SHT_SYMTAB_SHNDX section (if present).
__ndx must be within the number of symbols.
__sym must be a non-null pointer to writable GElf_Sym.
__xshndx must be a non-null pointer to writable Elf32_Word for the extended index.

functions.name: gelf_update_symshndx
functions.signature: extern int gelf_update_symshndx (Elf_Data *__symdata, Elf_Data *__shndxdata, int __ndx, GElf_Sym *__sym, Elf32_Word __xshndx);
functions.description: Updates a symbol table entry and its associated extended section index at index __ndx. Writes the symbol to __symdata and the extended index to __shndxdata. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: __symdata must be an Elf_Data for a writable symbol table.
__shndxdata must be an Elf_Data for the corresponding writable SHT_SYMTAB_SHNDX section (or appropriately handled if none).
__ndx must be within bounds of the symbol table.
__sym must be a non-null pointer to an initialized GElf_Sym.

functions.name: gelf_getsyminfo
functions.description: Retrieves the additional syminfo entry at index __ndx from a SHT_GNU_SYMINFOVER section (syminfo) into __dst as GElf_Syminfo. Returns __dst on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data from a syminfo section.
__ndx must be within the number of syminfo entries.
__dst must be a non-null pointer to writable GElf_Syminfo.

functions.name: gelf_update_syminfo
functions.description: Updates the syminfo entry at index __ndx from the provided GElf_Syminfo. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data for a writable syminfo section.
__ndx must be within bounds of the syminfo table.
__src must be a non-null pointer to an initialized GElf_Syminfo.

functions.name: gelf_getdyn
functions.description: Retrieves the dynamic table entry at index __ndx into __dst as a GElf_Dyn. Returns __dst on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data from a SHT_DYNAMIC section.
__ndx must be within the number of dynamic entries.
__dst must be a non-null pointer to writable GElf_Dyn.

functions.name: gelf_update_dyn
functions.description: Updates the dynamic table entry at index __ndx from the provided GElf_Dyn. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: __dst must be an Elf_Data for a writable dynamic section (SHT_DYNAMIC).
__ndx must be within bounds of the dynamic table.
__src must be a non-null pointer to an initialized GElf_Dyn.

functions.name: gelf_getmove
functions.description: Retrieves a move table entry at index __ndx into __dst as GElf_Move. Returns __dst on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data from a move table section (SHT_MOVE if present in toolchain).
__ndx must be within the number of move entries.
__dst must be a non-null pointer to writable GElf_Move.

functions.name: gelf_update_move
functions.description: Updates a move table entry at index __ndx from the provided GElf_Move. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data for a writable move section.
__ndx must be within bounds of the move table.
__src must be a non-null pointer to an initialized GElf_Move.

functions.name: gelf_getlib
functions.description: Retrieves a library list entry at index __ndx into __dst as GElf_Lib. Returns __dst on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data from a library list section (SHT_GNU_LIBLIST or similar).
__ndx must be within the number of library entries.
__dst must be a non-null pointer to writable GElf_Lib.

functions.name: gelf_update_lib
functions.description: Updates a library list entry at index __ndx from the provided GElf_Lib. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data for a writable library list section.
__ndx must be within bounds of the library table.
__src must be a non-null pointer to an initialized GElf_Lib.

functions.name: gelf_getversym
functions.description: Retrieves a version symbol (versym) entry at index __ndx into __dst as GElf_Versym. Returns __dst on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data from a SHT_GNU_versym section.
__ndx must be within the number of versym entries.
__dst must be a non-null pointer to writable GElf_Versym.

functions.name: gelf_update_versym
functions.description: Updates a version symbol entry at index __ndx from the provided GElf_Versym. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data for a writable versym section.
__ndx must be within bounds of the versym table.
__src must be a non-null pointer to an initialized GElf_Versym.

functions.name: gelf_getverneed
functions.description: Retrieves a required version (verneed) structure located at byte offset __offset within the data block into __dst as GElf_Verneed. Returns __dst on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data from a SHT_GNU_verneed section.
__offset must be a valid byte offset to a verneed entry within the data block, respecting alignment.
__dst must be a non-null pointer to writable GElf_Verneed.

functions.name: gelf_update_verneed
functions.description: Updates a required version (verneed) structure at byte offset __offset in the data block from the provided GElf_Verneed. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data for a writable verneed section.
__offset must point to a valid verneed entry location within the data.
__src must be a non-null pointer to an initialized GElf_Verneed.

functions.name: gelf_getvernaux
functions.description: Retrieves an auxiliary required version (vernaux) structure at byte offset __offset into __dst as GElf_Vernaux. Returns __dst on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data from a SHT_GNU_verneed section (aux entries live within verneed chains).
__offset must be a valid byte offset to a vernaux entry within the data.
__dst must be a non-null pointer to writable GElf_Vernaux.

functions.name: gelf_update_vernaux
functions.description: Updates an auxiliary required version (vernaux) structure at byte offset __offset from the provided GElf_Vernaux. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data for a writable verneed/vernaux data block.
__offset must point to a valid vernaux entry location within the data.
__src must be a non-null pointer to an initialized GElf_Vernaux.

functions.name: gelf_getverdef
functions.description: Retrieves a version definition (verdef) structure at byte offset __offset into __dst as GElf_Verdef. Returns __dst on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data from a SHT_GNU_verdef section.
__offset must be a valid byte offset to a verdef entry within the data.
__dst must be a non-null pointer to writable GElf_Verdef.

functions.name: gelf_update_verdef
functions.description: Updates a version definition (verdef) structure at byte offset __offset from the provided GElf_Verdef. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data for a writable verdef section.
__offset must point to a valid verdef entry location within the data.
__src must be a non-null pointer to an initialized GElf_Verdef.

functions.name: gelf_getverdaux
functions.description: Retrieves an auxiliary version definition (verdaux) structure at byte offset __offset into __dst as GElf_Verdaux. Returns __dst on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data from a SHT_GNU_verdef section (aux entries live within verdef chains).
__offset must be a valid byte offset to a verdaux entry within the data.
__dst must be a non-null pointer to writable GElf_Verdaux.

functions.name: gelf_update_verdaux
functions.description: Updates an auxiliary version definition (verdaux) structure at byte offset __offset from the provided GElf_Verdaux. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data for a writable verdef/verdaux data block.
__offset must point to a valid verdaux entry location within the data.
__src must be a non-null pointer to an initialized GElf_Verdaux.

functions.name: gelf_getauxv
functions.description: Retrieves an auxv entry at index __ndx into __dst as GElf_auxv_t. Returns __dst on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data from an auxiliary vector note or section containing auxv entries.
__ndx must be within the number of auxv entries present.
__dst must be a non-null pointer to writable GElf_auxv_t.

functions.name: gelf_update_auxv
functions.description: Updates an auxv entry at index __ndx from the provided GElf_auxv_t. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data for a writable auxv data block.
__ndx must be within bounds of the auxv table.
__src must be a non-null pointer to an initialized GElf_auxv_t.

functions.name: gelf_getnote
functions.signature: extern size_t gelf_getnote (Elf_Data *__data, size_t __offset, GElf_Nhdr *__result, size_t *__name_offset, size_t *__desc_offset);
functions.description: Parses a note starting at byte offset __offset within __data and fills __result with the note header and outputs the offsets of the note’s name and descriptor data. Returns the offset of the next note header on success, or 0 for an invalid offset or corrupt note header.
requirements: __data must be an Elf_Data from a SHT_NOTE section or PT_NOTE segment.
__offset must point to the start of a note header within the data; misaligned or out-of-range offsets cause a 0 return.
__result must be a non-null pointer to writable GElf_Nhdr.
__name_offset and __desc_offset must be non-null pointers to writable size_t to receive name and desc offsets.
Caller must check for a 0 return to detect invalid/corrupt notes.

functions.name: gelf_checksum
functions.description: Computes a simple checksum over the permanent parts of the ELF file represented by __elf. Returns the checksum value, or a negative value on error depending on libelf’s conventions.
requirements: __elf must be a valid Elf* representing an ELF file.
Caller should check for error indications per libelf (e.g., negative return) and consult elf_errno if needed.

functions.name: nlist
functions.description: Lookup symbol information from the given file and populate entries in the provided array of struct nlist. Intended usage is to prepare an array of nlist entries (typically with n_name set to the symbol names to query) and call nlist to fill in the remaining fields from the target file’s symbol table. Exact return semantics and array-termination conventions are not specified in this header; consult the specific library documentation. This function has C linkage and is part of elfutils.
requirements: __filename must be a valid, NUL-terminated path to a readable file.
The target file should be in a format supported by this implementation (elfutils typically expects ELF).
__nl must be a non-null pointer to a writable array of struct nlist.
Each element’s n_name should be initialized to the symbol name to be queried; other fields may be written by the function (inferred from typical nlist usage).
The array length/termination convention is not specified here; caller must follow the implementation’s documented convention (unknown in this header).
Thread-safety and reentrancy are not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: dwarf_begin
functions.description: Open a new libdw debug session on an ELF file descriptor. Use the returned Dwarf handle in subsequent queries and close with dwarf_end.
requirements: fildes must be a valid ELF file descriptor opened with appropriate access for cmd (DWARF_C_READ/DWARF_C_RDWR/DWARF_C_WRITE).
Caller must later call dwarf_end on the returned handle to release resources.

functions.name: dwarf_begin_elf
functions.description: Open a new libdw debug session on an existing libelf Elf handle. Returns a Dwarf handle for queries.
requirements: elf must be a valid, open Elf descriptor.
scngrp may select a section group; if non-NULL it must be a valid Elf_Scn from elf.
Caller must later call dwarf_end on the returned handle to release resources.

functions.name: dwarf_getelf
functions.description: Retrieve the underlying libelf Elf descriptor associated with a Dwarf handle.
requirements: dwarf must be a valid Dwarf session handle obtained from dwarf_begin/dwarf_begin_elf and not yet ended.

functions.name: dwarf_cu_getdwarf
functions.description: Retrieve the Dwarf session descriptor for the given compilation unit handle.
requirements: cu must be a valid Dwarf_CU associated with an active Dwarf session.

functions.name: dwarf_getalt
functions.description: Get the alternate DWARF descriptor used for .gnu_debugaltlink data for a main Dwarf session, or NULL if none set.
requirements: main must be a valid Dwarf session.
May return NULL if no alternate debug data is set.

functions.name: dwarf_setalt
functions.description: Attach an alternate DWARF descriptor to a main descriptor per .gnu_debugaltlink. Must be set before inspecting DIEs that might use alt FORMs (libdw otherwise tries to auto-set on first use).
requirements: main must be a valid Dwarf session.
alt must be a valid Dwarf session whose debug data matches MAIN (e.g., same build ID).
Caller must ensure ALT remains valid while used by MAIN until replaced by another dwarf_setalt or MAIN is ended.

functions.name: dwarf_end
functions.description: Release a Dwarf debug session and associated resources.
requirements: dwarf must be a Dwarf session previously returned by dwarf_begin/dwarf_begin_elf and not already ended.
After return, the handle and any pointers tied to it must not be used.

functions.name: dwarf_nextcu
functions.signature: extern int dwarf_nextcu (Dwarf *dwarf, Dwarf_Off off, Dwarf_Off *next_off, size_t *header_sizep, Dwarf_Off *abbrev_offsetp, uint8_t *address_sizep, uint8_t *offset_sizep) __nonnull_attribute__ (3);
functions.description: Read the header of the next DWARF compilation unit (.debug_info). Returns 0 on success, 1 when done, or -1 on error.
requirements: next_off must be non-NULL (nonnull(3)).
If non-NULL, header_sizep, abbrev_offsetp, address_sizep, offset_sizep receive header fields.
off is the offset to start reading from (use 0 initially).
dwarf must be a valid session.

functions.name: dwarf_next_unit
functions.signature: extern int dwarf_next_unit (Dwarf *dwarf, Dwarf_Off off, Dwarf_Off *next_off, size_t *header_sizep, Dwarf_Half *versionp, Dwarf_Off *abbrev_offsetp, uint8_t *address_sizep, uint8_t *offset_sizep, uint64_t *type_signaturep, Dwarf_Off *type_offsetp) __nonnull_attribute__ (3);
functions.description: Read the header of the next DWARF unit (CU or type unit). If type_signaturep is non-NULL reads a type unit; otherwise reads a CU. Returns 0 on success, 1 when done, or -1 on error.
requirements: next_off must be non-NULL (nonnull(3)).
Off is the starting offset; use 0 initially.
Optional output pointers may be NULL to skip results.
dwarf must be valid.

functions.name: dwarf_get_units
functions.signature: extern int dwarf_get_units (Dwarf *dwarf, Dwarf_CU *cu, Dwarf_CU **next_cu, Dwarf_Half *version, uint8_t *unit_type, Dwarf_Die *cudie, Dwarf_Die *subdie) __nonnull_attribute__ (3);
functions.description: Iterate over Dwarf units, providing version, unit type and (if available) CU and subtype DIEs. Returns 0 on success, 1 if no more units, -1 on error.
requirements: next_cu must be non-NULL (nonnull(3)).
To start iteration pass cu as NULL; otherwise pass previous next_cu.
Output pointers may be NULL to skip fields; if unavailable they may be cleared by the function.

functions.name: dwarf_cu_info
functions.signature: extern int dwarf_cu_info (Dwarf_CU *cu, Dwarf_Half *version, uint8_t *unit_type, Dwarf_Die *cudie, Dwarf_Die *subdie, uint64_t *unit_id, uint8_t *address_size, uint8_t *offset_size);
functions.description: Fetch metadata and DIEs associated with the given Dwarf_CU. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error. Arguments not needed can be NULL; missing info won't be looked up.
requirements: cu must be a valid CU handle.
If the unit type has no sub DIE, subdie will be cleared.
If there is no unit_id, it will be set to zero.

functions.name: dwarf_next_cfi
functions.signature: extern int dwarf_next_cfi (const unsigned char e_ident[], Elf_Data *data, bool eh_frame_p, Dwarf_Off offset, Dwarf_Off *next_offset, Dwarf_CFI_Entry *entry) __nonnull_attribute__ (1, 2, 5, 6);
functions.description: Decode one CFI entry (CIE or FDE) from raw section data (either .eh_frame or .debug_frame). Returns 0 on success (entry filled), 1 when no more (next_offset set to (Dwarf_Off)-1), or -1 on error (may still advance next_offset).
requirements: e_ident must be non-NULL and correspond to the originating ELF e_ident (for address size/endian).

functions.description: Access the CFI from the DWARF .debug_frame section. Returns NULL if absent. Pointer valid until dwarf_end on the Dwarf; must not be passed to dwarf_cfi_end. Repeated calls return the same pointer.

requirements: elf must be a valid open Elf descriptor.
Caller must call dwarf_cfi_end on the returned pointer before calling elf_end on elf.

functions.name: dwarf_cfi_end
functions.description: Release resources allocated by dwarf_getcfi_elf for a CFI cache.
requirements: cache must be a pointer previously returned by dwarf_getcfi_elf and not yet freed.

functions.name: dwarf_offdie
functions.description: Return the DIE at a given .debug_info offset into result and return result. Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: dwarf_offdie_types
functions.description: Return the DIE at a given .debug_types offset into result and return result. Returns NULL on failure.

functions.signature: extern Dwarf_Die *dwarf_cu_die (Dwarf_CU *cu, Dwarf_Die *result, Dwarf_Half *versionp, Dwarf_Off *abbrev_offsetp, uint8_t *address_sizep, uint8_t *offset_sizep, uint64_t *type_signaturep, Dwarf_Off *type_offsetp) __nonnull_attribute__ (2);

functions.description: Iterate attributes of DIE starting at given byte offset, calling callback for each until DWARF_CB_OK stops or end. Returns offset of offending attribute, 1 at end, or -1 on error.

functions.name: dwarf_tag

functions.name: dwarf_attr

functions.description: Decode an attribute as a signed constant. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: dwarf_formflag
functions.description: Return the boolean flag value of an attribute. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: dwarf_diename
functions.description: Return the DW_AT_name string of a DIE or NULL if absent/error.

functions.description: Return the abbreviation tag (DW_TAG_*).

functions.description: Return nonzero if the abbreviation has the children flag set.

functions.description: Get number of attributes in an abbreviation. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

cudie must be a CU DIE.

functions.name: dwarf_onesrcline
functions.description: Return a pointer to the idx-th line record from a Dwarf_Lines table.

functions.name: dwarf_getsrcfiles
functions.description: Get the list of source files used in the CU. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

cudie must be a CU DIE.
nfiles may be NULL to skip count.

functions.name: dwarf_getsrc_die
functions.description: Find the source line entry for an address within a CU. Returns a Dwarf_Line or NULL if not found/error.

functions.name: dwarf_lineepiloguebegin
functions.description: Return whether the line record marks the beginning of a function epilogue. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: dwarf_lineisa
functions.description: Return the instruction-set architecture code for a line record. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

mtime and length may be NULL.

functions.name: dwarf_line_file
functions.description: Return the Dwarf_Files and index corresponding to a Dwarf_Line. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

line must be valid.

functions.name: dwarf_getsrcdirs
functions.signature: extern int dwarf_getsrcdirs (Dwarf_Files *files, const char *const **result, size_t *ndirs) __nonnull_attribute__ (2, 3);
functions.description: Return the list of include directories used in the file table. (*result)[0] is the CU's DW_AT_comp_dir and may be null. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
